headline: Referred data center zoning ordinance and parking ordinance to Planning Board; approved $920,836.00 fiscal 2026 budget transfer; rent stabilization resolution passed 9-2.
summary: The council referred a data center zoning ordinance and a parking ordinance to the Planning Board for joint public hearings. It approved $920,836.00 to close out fiscal year 2026 and adopted a resolution urging support for rent stabilization by a 9-2 vote. It confirmed several board appointments and granted block party and license requests.
decisions: Granted National Grid's location to install conduits on North Street at Bryant Street.
Confirmed Dr. Javier Garcia-Perez to the Race Equity Commission, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Confirmed the re-appointments of Kirt Rieder to the Planning Board and Peter Habib to the Zoning Board of Appeals, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Confirmed Elena Eimert to the Planning Board, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Confirmed Phillip Pelletier to the Salem Harbor Port Authority, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Confirmed the appointments of Ellen Simpson and Hilary Forbes to the Zoning Board of Appeals and Emmet Costen to the Conservation Commission, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Appropriated $920,836.00 to close out fiscal year 2026.
Appropriated $42,309.00 from the General Stabilization Fund to the Fire Department for a comprehensive manning study.
Appropriated $38,117.89 from the Golf Course receipts account to buy HD300 Select Spray equipment.
Appropriated $14,430.00 from the Salem Common receipts account to paint the Salem Common light posts.
Allowed $442.86 in fiscal year 2025 Engineering invoices to be paid from the fiscal year 2026 budget, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Allowed $176.89 in fiscal year 2023 Building Department invoices to be paid from the fiscal year 2026 budget, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Authorized the Mayor to enter an easement agreement with South River Partnership LLC for 315 Derby Street and to end the easement with Beverly Cooperative Bank, 10 yeas, 0 nays, 1 absent.
Referred the data center zoning ordinance to the Planning Board to hold a joint public hearing.
Adopted an order asking the Committee on Ordinances, Licenses and Legal Affairs to meet and create a zoning ordinance on roof-mounted wind energy systems.
Referred the zoning ordinance on required parking spaces, parking and loading, and development standards to the Planning Board to hold a joint public hearing.
Accepted the Community and Economic Development Committee report and adopted its recommendation on the rent stabilization resolution.
Adopted two amendments to the rent stabilization resolution proposed by Councillor King.
Withdrew Councillor Sydoriak's original amendment to the rent stabilization resolution and proposed a revised amendment.
Failed to adopt Councillor Sydoriak's revised amendment to the rent stabilization resolution, 3 yeas, 7 nays, 1 present, 0 absent.
Adopted the rent stabilization resolution as amended, 9 yeas, 2 nays, 0 absent.
Accepted the Government Services Committee report and adopted its recommendation to confirm Annie Thompson and re-appoint Kate Martin to the Community Preservation Committee.
Confirmed Annie Thompson to the Community Preservation Committee for a one-year term ending July 9, 2027, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Confirmed the re-appointment of Kate Martin to the Community Preservation Committee, term ending May 23, 2028, 11 yeas, 0 nays, 0 absent.
Ordered a hearing for September 10, 2026 on National Grid's petition to install conduits on Essex Street at Essex and Flint Streets.
Granted the residents' request for a block party on Linden and Wisteria Streets on August 9, 2026.
Granted the Clark Street block party request for September 12, 2026.
Granted the Lemon Street Court block party request for July 25, 2026.
Granted the Warner Street block party request for September 6, 2026.
Granted the listed public guide and taxi operator license applications.
Referred the listed claims to the Committee on Ordinances, Licenses and Legal Affairs.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council was held in-person on Thursday, July 9, 2026 at

President Merkl requested that everyone who is able to please rise to recite the Pledge 
of Allegiance. 
 
Salem City Council Land Acknowledgement 
 
The Salem City Council honors that this land is Naumkeag, or fishing place, where 
generations of Naumkeag people from the Pawtucket band of the Massachusett Tribe 
lived and passed through for centuries. 
 
We acknowledge that this is unceded Indigenous land and also acknowledge the 
Massachusett Tribe, who continue to honor and hold this land into the present. 
 
Salem’s City Council is committed to having ongoing meaningful dialogue with the 
indigenous peoples who have presence in Salem in order to dismantle the legacies of 
oppression and inequities that persist today.

#388 - (#362) - RENT STABILIZATION RESOLUTION 
 
Councillor Prosniewski offered the following report for the Committee on Community 
and Economic Development co-posted with the Committee of the Whole. It was voted 
to accept the report and adopt the recommendation. 
 
The Committee on Community and Economic Development co-posted with the 
Committee of the Whole to whom was referred the matter of a Resolution To Urge 
Support for Rent Stabilization To Protect Tenants and Preserve Our Community has 
considered said matter and would recommend that the Resolution be adopted as 
amended by a roll call vote. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Use 
Dwellings, two-family; Dwellings, 
multifamily 
Required Parking 
None
11 
CITY OF SALEM 
JULY 9, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
 
Councillor King commented that the committee had about a two and a half hour meeting 
that included a presentation from Carolyn Chu, the executive director of Homes for All 
Massachusetts, as well as significant comment from the public and discussion among 
the Councillors. I would say I was especially impressed with how clear it was that 
amongst both the council and the public, the obvious passion for addressing the 
housing crisis that we have here in Salem is the rising costs of housing and the severe 
number of Salem residents who are cost burdened by the cost of their rent.  We did 
make two amendments to the resolution through the course of the discussion, just to 
make the resolution more consistent with the reality of like the legislative session and 
what's going on in the legislature. 
 
Councillor King stated that the two amendments were as follows to add the language 
that is bolded and delete the language that has lines through it: 
 
WHEREAS, a proposed initiative petition for the November 2026 ballot has been 
struck down by the Supreme Judicial Court, leaving only legislation currently under 
consideration by the Massachusetts Legislature to seek to enable rent stabilization 
policies, including limiting annual rent increases based on a formula accounting for 
the Consumer Price Index with a cap of 5%; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council hereby 
expresses its strong support for the legislation entitled "An Act enabling cities and 
towns to stabilize rents and protect tenants" in favor of lifting the ban on rent 
stabilization statewide; and 
 
Councillor Smith seconded the motion to accept the amendments. 
 
The amendments stated above were adopted.   
 
Councillor Prosniewski motioned to adopt the resolution as amended.  
 
Council Holappa - I think this is important that the Council consider using our voice here 
to stand up for our community. We have an opportunity as leaders in this community, as 
legislators here to recognize something that is not necessarily within our control, but 
something that could be very valuable to the people in this city and there might be some 
negative consequences to that I think folks have rightfully pointed out to us but that 
doesn't mean that there is nothing that we can do to address those. There is no silver 
bullet when it comes to addressing the housing crisis. And I believe that we should be, 
this body should be using our voice to advocate to have as many tools in our toolbox as 
we can to address this urgent crisis.
12 
CITY OF SALEM 
JULY 9, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
 
Councillor Sydoriak -  I was actually the one that voted no coming out of the committee. 
That is because mostly I had difficulty wanting to be a yes vote because of procedural 
reasons and then also I am very worried about the unintended consequences of this bill 
or policy. I think it's really important to have this tool, but I think it's crucial to have a 
holistic approach, and I really appreciate all the care that was brought forward through 
all the Councillors and the public when we are having that conversation on Monday and 
towards the end of that conversation, there's a few ideas coming up that could help try 
to support rent stabilization with those unintended consequences. I really didn't have 
time to come up with some thoughts to add to the resolution then, but it took some time 
since then that could be added to the resolution that I think would make this approach 
stronger and embraces our desire to help out people in Salem using every single tool 
that we have. I would like offer a motion to amend this to so that we have that spirit of 
tackling this really difficult and complicated issue in a holistic way. I move to insert 
language by adding  two paragraphs,  
 
   “WHEREAS, stabilizing rents serves as an immediate safety net to prevent tenant 
displacement, and must be paired with proactive local and state policies that actively unlock 
new housing production to permanently resolve the structural supply crisis driving Salem’s, and 
Massachusetts housing shortage; and  
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council hereby expresses support for other 
efforts that enable more housing production; and therefore expresses its strong support for the 
core housing objectives that Massachusetts legislators are working to  incorporate in “An Act 
relative to economic development in the commonwealth,” House Bill 5562, collectively urging 
the Legislature to pass comprehensive reforms that dismantle restrictive zoning barriers to 
multi-family housing, streamline development timelines, and empower faith-based institutions to 
utilize their land as-of-right for affordable housing production; and to express the City Council's 
support for allowing single-family homes on small lots in areas with adequate infrastructure, 
recognizing its potential to facilitate the production of needed housing on smaller lots throughout 
the Commonwealth.” 
This motion was seconded by Councillor Turowski. 
 
Councill Holappa, I don't like to stand on procedure very often. But there was a full 10 
days between this when this was sent to committee, and when the committee meeting 
was had, and while I don't necessarily disagree, I think, with any of the language that 
was there I'm just not comfortable voting to put that in here, and I'm not exactly sure 
where the intent on those would be to go. I tend to be a very visual person with these 
sorts of things, so I would have been more comfortable had this been brought to the 
committee, and we had had that discussion then rather than adding these at this point.
13 
CITY OF SALEM 
JULY 9, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
 
Councilor King. I also agree with the sentiment of what is written in this language, 
though I do also take procedural issue with it. The resolution is titled to urge support for 
rent stabilization to protect our tenants and preserve our community. And while the 
things proposed would also protect our tenants and preserve our community to some 
degree. This is not consistent with the rest of the language of the resolution. I do agree 
that a 2.5 hour meeting with 10 days notice is ample time to pre-draft amendments, and 
I will also say I think sometimes we have to take controversial votes and watering down 
the language to throw a lot of things in there so you can feel more comfortable taking a 
vote.  It's a choice. It's not one that I feel like we need to take… I think people should 
just take a vote on something that we've been talking about for two weeks.  I love all of 
those ideas, and I think we could bring in another resolution. We could bring in more 
specific zoning changes that address the specific types of concerns that are in there. 
We are able to do all of that.
